title: Google Translate API Pricing: Cost Per Million (2026)
summary: Google Translate API pricing costs $20 per million characters, with 500,000 free characters included each month.
body_markdown:
## Control hidden costs affecting translation bills


Because several charges and limits sit outside your character count, it's only the starting point, and each one widens the gap between your estimate and the invoice.


### How characters are counted and billed


Google counts characters of text sent, so spaces and punctuation count. Words and bytes don't enter into it.


If you send HTML, the **markup tags count too** , which means a templated email can cost noticeably more than the visible copy suggests. Strip the tags or send only the strings that need translating.


When a nightly job retranslates a whole product catalog, it pays for the untouched rows each run. The API doesn't know that a string is unchanged since yesterday, so **Google bills every resend as new text** .


Cache results keyed on the source string and translate only what changed.


When a large document runs into the size ceiling on each request or the per-minute character quota on each project, it has to be split into batches and paced.


Batching adds retry logic, and a retry after a partial failure can bill the same characters twice. Budget for that overlap rather than assuming a clean single pass.


### Add-on charges beyond translation itself


If you detect first and then translate, Google meters the same text twice, because language detection is a separate call billed on its own characters. Where you already know the source language, skip detection.


Glossaries and custom models also carry their own charges, so check whether the accuracy gain justifies a second line item.


Automation multiplies this. A connector library such as the one below, listing 502 integrations, shows how many triggers can feed text into a translation step: a webhook, a spreadsheet row, an incoming email, meaning your translation workflows can start from virtually any tool.


Every one of those is a path that can resend text without anyone noticing.


Even free usage requires a billing account, so you attach a card from day one. Create a budget with threshold alerts in the billing console, then check the quota page to see the per-minute limits applied to your project.


**An alert only notifies you, so pair it with a quota cap if you need a hard stop.**
